newsitem.title: SPAIN: Two more face Banesto bank fraud charges in Spain.
newsitem.headline: Two more face Banesto bank fraud charges in Spain.

text.p: Two associates of disgraced financier Mario Conde, the former chairman of Spain's Banesto bank, will face fraud charges, court sources said on Tuesday.

High Court Judge Luis Lopez asked on Monday for charges to be brought against Conde's lawyer Mariano Gomez de Liano and business associate Francisco Sitges on suspicion they ran a network of Swiss companies which diverted funds from Banesto.

Conde was formally charged in May with fraud, misappropriation of funds and use of false procedures following a 16-month investigation into the 1993 collapse of Banco Espanol de Credito-Banesto, Spain's biggest financial crime case.
Liano is the brother of Javier Gomez de Liano, a prominent high court judge who is trying one of the key cases in Spain's 1980s "dirty war" against the Basque separatist group ETA.
Sitges, former chairman of Spanish zinc producer Asturiana de Zinc, and Liano are expected to be formally charged by the court within days, the sources said.
With the new charges, a total of nine former senior officials of Banesto will face prosecution.

Conde is accused by politicians of having bought thousands of stolen military intelligence files and leaking them to Spanish media with deliberate regularity to incriminate former officials and enemies.
Leading Spanish newspapers published some of the secret documents this week.
The daily El Mundo said the papers showed the former Socialist government ran death squads that targeted ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) rebels and killed 28 people from 1983-1987.
